title: Decision mimid-1wgh.120 is wrong at the provider: suppressing the Chat removes the room's messages
description:
Found 2026-11-23 while implementing decision mimid-1wgh.120, by reading
the code before changing it. The decision, and the spec text pushed for
it (jmap-chat-spec 0f187aa), are wrong about WHERE the Chat is
suppressed.

WHAT I CHECKED. In mimid-server, every JMAP message projection INNER
JOINs follower_chat:

  store/jmap.rs message_columns!(): "FROM follower_event e JOIN
  follower_chat c ON c.room_id = e.room_id AND c.user_uri = ?1"

and the per-Chat message id query does the same. So a room with no
follower_chat row has no messages visible through the provider's JMAP API
at all. The agent would never receive anything sent in a call room,
including the SDP signalling of bead mimid-1wgh.114.5. Suppressing the
Chat does not hide a conversation; it deletes the channel.

AND THE DRAFT SAYS SO, in the section next to the one I edited.
§Chat.roomId: "A Chat with a roomId has kind group. Its participant list,
roles, and metadata are MLS group state ... and its messages are sent
with Room/send". The Chat IS the room's message container and the MLS
client's handle on it. I edited §Room/create without reading
§Chat.roomId, which is the second time today that reading one section and
not its neighbour produced a wrong answer.

ALSO WRONG EVEN IF IT WORKED: a follower cannot tell. §5 puts a
parent-dependent room on the same hub as its parent, so the CREATOR's
provider is the hub and can read the policy. Every other participant's
provider is a follower, holds no group state, and cannot decrypt the
Welcome, so it cannot know the room is parent-dependent. The rule was
unenforceable for every participant but one.

WHERE THE RULE ACTUALLY BELONGS. mimid has two JMAP endpoints with
different audiences:

- THE PROVIDER'S (mimid-server), consumed by the AGENT, which is an MLS
  member and knows what the room is. The Chat here is addressing. It must
  stay.
- THE AGENT'S OWN (mimid-agent-jmap), consumed by a STOCK HUMAN CLIENT.
  Here a Chat is a PROJECTION of the store's record::Room
  (render.rs new_chat, keyed by room.key), and the store keeps the room
  and its messages whether or not a Chat is projected. Omitting one loses
  nothing, and this is the endpoint where the mystery-empty-chat problem
  actually appears.

So: the provider keeps binding a Chat, and the agent's front end does not
project a call room as one. Room::parent already marks which rooms.

WHAT TO FIX IN THE PUSHED DRAFT (needs Mark's OK, like any write there):
revert the no-Chat sentence and the chatId (Id|null) change of 0f187aa in
§Room/create, and instead give the Chat a way to SAY what it is, so a
client can tell rather than the server hiding it: a parentRoomId field
beside roomId in §Chat.roomId, null for an ordinary room. A client that
knows the field hides or badges the Chat; mimid's agent front end filters
on it. Say plainly why the Chat cannot simply be omitted: it is the
room's message container.

DECISION mimid-1wgh.120 SHOULD BE REOPENED OR SUPERSEDED. Its reasoning
("a call is a VTCCall; the call room is its keying substrate, not a
conversation") survives; its mechanism does not.
close_reason: Specs fixed and pushed (jmap-chat-spec a756342): the Chat stays, parentRoomId tells a client what it is, and the suppression moves to the agent's front end.
